name: DBAF (DB bicarbonate mineral medium + acetate + fumarate) (PMC11972089)
description: DBAF (DB bicarbonate mineral medium + acetate + fumarate) — medium reported in PMC11972089, extracted for GrowthDB and mapped to BiGG.

provenance.citation: Medium composition from PMC11972089 (see GrowthDB record).
provenance.notes: Composition mapped to BiGG (mapper + salt dissociation); presence-based bounds; paper_amount retained. Added via GrowthDB curation.
provenance.verification: paper-verified (complete recipe; cited + supplementary sources chased)
provenance.verification_evidence: Per liter of deionized water: ... 2.5 g NaHCO3 ... Gas phase 80% Ar-20% CO2
provenance.base_medium: DB = bicarbonate-buffered freshwater mineral medium (Reguera/Lovley Geobacter lineage) + 20 mM Na-acetate + 40 mM Na-fumarate (DBAF), reduced with 2 mM cysteine under N2:CO2 80:20

sources_chased.what: ref 39 = Speers & Reguera 2012 AEM 78:437 (PMC3255729), cited as the DB medium source
added: confirms DB = anaerobic mineral medium + 10 mL/L vitamin mix; cites Srikanth 2008 (ref38) for mineral base and Balch 1979 (ref1) for vitamins

sources_chased.what: Geobacter freshwater (FW) base-salt recipe (Coppi et al 2001 AEM 67:3180, PMC92998; same Reguera/Lovley lineage)
Wolfe/Wolin trace mineral solution + vitamin solution constituent list (DSMZ Medium 141; Balch 1979 lineage)
added: 15 trace-mineral salts incl. NTA, Fe, Mn, Co, Zn, Cu, Ni, Mo, B, Al, Se, W
10 vitamins incl. biotin, thiamine, B12, riboflavin, pantothenate, PABA, lipoic acid

missing_before: Trace mineral constituents (nitrilotriacetic acid, MgSO4, MnSO4, NaCl, FeSO4, CoSO4, CaCl2, ZnSO4, CuSO4, AlK(SO4)2, H3BO3, Na2MoO4, NiCl2, Na2SeO3, Na2WO4)
Vitamin constituents (biotin, folic acid, pyridoxine, thiamine, riboflavin, nicotinic acid, Ca-pantothenate, B12, PABA, lipoic acid)
recuration.notes: DBAF main text gives only the modifications (acetate/fumarate/cysteine/gas/bicarbonate) and cites ref 39 (Speers & Reguera 2012) for the base DB medium; that paper in turn cites Srikanth 2008 for the mineral base and Balch 1979 for vitamins. The scanned base papers were not machine-extractable, so the base salt concentrations are taken from the canonical, verbatim-published Geobacter freshwater medium of the same lab lineage (Coppi et al 2001), and the trace-mineral/vitamin constituents from the standard Wolfe/Wolin (Balch 1979) solutions as codified in DSMZ Medium 141 (both dosed 10 mL/L).
